A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GALLa and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D. Despite extensive reformatting, corresponding content can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original fine-tuning experiments across five code tasks, with seven LLM configurations, ablations, statistical tests, and an example model output.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Tables 3–6 and the statistical tests and model-output example in Appendices C–D.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the GNN–adapter–LLM architecture, Graph2Code and GraphQA objectives, two-stage training procedure, and removal of graph modules at inference. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use CodeNet for Python/Java graph alignment, CodefuseEval for translation, and CodeXGLUE for clone detection, defect detection, summarization, and repair. The represented languages and task coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 6 newly includes the downstream-only Phi-1 baseline as an explicit comparator for the MLP and MagNet variants. This baseline already appears in Table 3, so the change is limited to comparator membership in this reported comparison.

E3.justification: Dataset counts, preprocessing, metrics, multi-task and single-task settings, training budgets, checkpoint selection, and model configurations remain unchanged. Removal of the hyperparameter-search disclosure does not establish a changed experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the AST/DFG, code-only, adapter, and graph-encoder ablations, the preliminary GraphQA analyses, and the single-task hallucination example. The repeated baseline in Table 6 introduces no new ablation or robustness test.

E5.justification: Appendix C retains the same chi-squared and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, and Table 3 retains the p < 0.1 significance convention. No repeated-run, seed, or uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Existing scores in Tables 3–6 and p-values in Table 9 match across versions, as do the qualitative findings and Figure 7 output. The added Table 6 baseline reproduces the existing Table 3 Phi-1 scores, including the 41.4 average.

T1.justification: Equations 1–2, the training probability expressions, and the structural-graph definitions in Appendix A are unchanged. No formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about model/task independence, graph alignment without additional inference cost, and effectiveness across five tasks and seven LLM configurations. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 deletes the Limitations section, including discussion of restricted large-model validation, the rationale for using directly fine-tuned LLM baselines, and the absence of individual task hyperparameter searches. Interpretations of cross-language transfer, ablations, and single-task failures remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds title-page code and dataset links ending in '/xxx', while retaining the GALLa-specific links in the introduction. It also removes the explicit disclosure that individual task hyperparameter searches were not conducted; the remaining implementation details and appendix prompts are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and Section 2 comparisons are retained, with bibliographic metadata and formatting changes only. However, deleting Limitations removes the explicit claim to be the first graph-enhanced decoder-only LLM work and its stated positioning as a baseline for future research.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged. v3 removes Limitations, Ethical Statements, and Acknowledgments, and revises author/contact information and bibliography formatting; there is little substantive rewriting of the retained narrative.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the two-column design with a predominantly single-column layout, adds CodeFuse running headers and branding, and extensively resizes and relocates displays. Tables 1, 7, and 8 wrap alongside text, Table 6 gains a baseline row, and appendix displays are grouped more closely with their explanations.

improvement.justification: Displaying the existing baseline in Table 6 and grouping appendix displays with their explanations offer modest presentation benefits. However, v3 removes substantive limitations and introduces prominent placeholder resource links, despite retaining the GALLa-specific links elsewhere. With the scientific evidence unchanged, these losses in transparency and access clarity outweigh the limited presentation gains.
